correctness.rationale: Complete proof for exactly \(2^{14}\) binary words: each observation is bijective with its integer array \(c_{\ell,r}\) of prefix-sum differences, and every word is visited exactly once. Python and independently written C++ enumerate all 16,384 words, grouping on exact tuple/vector equality, and agree on 128 singleton, 8104 two-word and 12 four-word fibers (total 8244). They agree member-for-member on the twelve explicit quadruples; the maximum is therefore exactly four. The lower bound is realized by listed words; no generalization from samples is asserted.

value.rationale: The first case where \(n+1\) has two distinct odd prime factors lies outside source exact families. Determining \(E_{14}\)=4, rather than the previously permitted 4 or 8, closes a motivated natural ambiguity-bound gap. Exhaustive equality classification quantifies every nonreconstructable sequence (48/16384=3/1024) for the original composition-observation channel. Its utility is an exact worst-case finite reconstruction benchmark, independent of any asserted asymptotic extension.
